'''''Spiranthes aestivalis''''', commonly called the '''summer lady's-tresses''', is a species of [[orchid]] found in western Europe, Turkey, Russia, and North Africa. The [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]], ''aestivalis'', is derived from [[Latin]] and means "pertaining to the summer".<ref name="Eggli Newton 2004">{{cite book |last=Eggli |first=Urs |last2=Newton |first2=Leonard E. |title=Etymological Dictionary of Succulent Plant Names |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |year=2004 |isbn=978-3-540-00489-9 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=u2n5vusQ1DEC&pg=PA4 |access-date=12 November 2018 |page=4}}</ref>

It has become [[local extinction|locally extinct]] in the [[British Isles]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jacob |first1=Ben |title=My law-breaking mission to save Britain’s endangered orchids |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2023/jul/02/my-law-breaking-mission-to-save-britains-endangered-orchids-ben-jacob |access-date=2 July 2023 |work=The Observer |date=2 July 2023}}</ref>
